text: Love and Hate are two of the most used, abused, and misused words of mankind.

author: Jacque Fresco
text: If you think we can't change the world, it just means you're not one of those who will.

author: A.J. Beirens
text: Nothing remains the same.The only thing that never changesis the fact that everything changes.

author: Magnus Nwagu Amudi
text: In life, everything is built. Have you thought about it. You built who you are, how you want to be perceived, you built your character, you chose to remain where you are, you are your own creator. You can choose to be something else. You are not what you were, you can be anything you choose to build.

author: Daniel Egger
text: Our reality defines itself by people who strive for change

author: Amit Chatterjee
text: Success comes from people (leaders) who are motivated by the change, not who need to be motivated by the change.

author: P. Wish
text: When a memory dies, the truth takes its place. Losing a memory is more painful than losing an arm. Because memories cannot be amputated. In familiarity, we find a sense of security. When this security leaves, the unfamiliar remains.

author: Elizabeth Esguerra Castillo
text: To be truly free is to liberate yourself from worries. To have peace despite chaos engulfing your world, to let go and let God. To live one day at a time and to embrace the winds of change and not to chase what is not meant to be yours. To just wait patiently for God's Divine Timing and to savor the moment each day has to offer.

author: Colleen Ferrary Bader
text: When will you stop doing what you’ve always done and start doing what you can to begin to live the life you deserve?It’s Time. You’ve got this.

author: Saim Cheeda
text: How do we perceive what’s important in life, from what we once thought to what we think now, how does it change?

author: Ufuoma Apoki
text: Keep living the best you could possibly offer life. You might not literally change the world if that's your original dream, but you would change, inspire, and make a difference in one person's world with the best of your world. Then you'd realize the truth that, one is too many.That, my dear, is the right step in the direction of changing the world.

author: Alex Haditaghi
text: Sometimes when you try to change the world, the world changes you!

author: Susan Sontag
text: I must change my life so that I can live it, not wait for it.

author: Dionna L. Hayden
text: If we want to see real change in our world, it begins with us all on an individual basis.

author: Dionna L. Hayden
text: Some of the greatest miracles one could ever receive in their life is the ones that happen when their faith and action has been applied.

author: Asuni LadyZeal
text: Change is often overrated: at times, all you need to change is how you change what you change in your life.

author: Donna Goddard
text: Faith changes us - faith in something intrinsically good, something other than ourselves, something bigger than ourselves.

author: Jimmy Carter
text: We cannot change the history of the past.

author: Nike Thaddeus
text: Don't keep your nation-changing thoughts to yourself. Else it won't actually change the nation. Impact!

author: Constance Chuks Friday
text: Stop being okay with the norm, seek to transform.

author: Kayko Tamaki
text: Security is merely an illusion.If you think your schedule, your botox, your insurance, your marriage certificate, your 401K, and the deadbolt on your door is going to keep you safe from change and the happenings of life—think again. Nothing is guaranteed. Nothing can give you solid ground but your own trust in yourself and the purpose of existing-- That is the only solid ground upon which you can stand.

author: Elisabeth Kübler-Ross
text: Should you shield the canyons from the windstorms you would never see the true beauty of their carvings.

author: Edgar Allan Poe
text: Beauty of whatever kind, in its supreme development, invariably excites the sensitive soul to tears.

author: Albert Einstein
text: Our task must be to free ourselves... by widening our circle of compassion to embrace all living creatures and the whole of nature and it's beauty.

author: Thich Nhat Hanh
text: The mind can go in a thousand directions, but on this beautiful path, I walk in peace. With each step, the wind blows. With each step, a flower blooms.

author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
text: Many eyes go through the meadow, but few see the flowers in it

author: Robinson Jeffers
text: The greatest beauty is organic wholeness, the wholeness of life and things, the divine beauty of the universe.

author: Naomi Wolf
text: Is the beauty myth good to men? It hurts them by teaching them how to avoid loving women. It prevents men from actually seeing women. It does not, contrary to its own professed ideology, stimulate and gratify sexual longing. In suggesting a vision in place of a woman, it has a numbing effect, reducing all senses but the visual, and impairing even that.

author: Cheri K. Erdman
text: Healthy emotions come in all sizes. Healthy minds come in all sizes. And healthy bodies come in all sizes.

author: Naomi Wolf
text: A cultural fixation on female thinness is not an obsession about female beauty but an obsession about female obedience.

author: Jason Letts
text: I used to think that if I were a certain kind of person I would spend all my time creating something beautiful. Well, it turns out I am, and I am.

author: C.S. Lewis
text: We do not want merely to see beauty... we want something else which can hardly be put into words- to be united with the beauty we see, to pass into it, to receive it into ourselves, to bathe in it, to become part of it. That is why we have peopled air and earth and water with gods and goddesses, and nymphs and elves.

author: Naomi Wolf
text: No matter what a woman's appearance may be, it will be used to undermine what she is saying and taken to individualize - as her personal problem - observations she makes about the beauty myth in society.

author: John Muir
text: A few minutes ago every tree was excited, bowing to the roaring storm,waving, swirling, tossing their branches in glorious enthusiasm likeworship. But though to the outer ear these trees are now silent, theirsongs never cease. -John Muir, naturalist, explorer, and writer (1838-1914)

author: Piper Payne
text: There is something beautiful about a blank canvas, the nothingness of the beginning that is so simple and breathtakingly pure. It’s the paint that changes its meaning and the hand that creates the story. Every piece begins the same, but in the end they are all uniquely different.

author: Susan Sarandon
text: Ladies, stress shows on your face. Happiness is the true beauty we

author: Alain de Botton
text: You normally have to be bashed about a bit by life to see the point of daffodils, sunsets and uneventful nice days.

author: Don Marquis
text: fire is beautifuland we know that if we gettoo close it will kill usbut what does that matterit is better to be happy for a momentand be burned up with beautythan to live a long timeand be bored all the while

author: Hayao Miyazaki
text: Yet, even amidst the hatred and carnage, life is still worth living. It is possible for wonderful encounters and beautiful things to exist.

author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
text: Things are pretty, graceful, rich, elegant, handsome, but, until they speak to the imagination, not yet beautiful.

author: Naomi Wolf
text: Beauty' is a currency system like the gold standard. Like any economy, it is determined by politics, and in the modern age in the West is is the last, best belief system that keeps male dominance intact.

author: Naomi Wolf
text: Most urgently, women's identity must be premised upon our "beauty" so that we will remain vulnerable to outside approval, carrying the vital sensitive organ of self-esteem exposed to the air.

author: Dejan Stojanovic
text: It is beautiful to talk about beautiful things and even more beautiful to silently gaze at them.

author: Bernard DeVoto
text: One may lack words to express the impact of beauty but no one who has felt it remains untouched. It is renewal, enlargement, intensification. The parks preserve it permanently in the inheritance of the American citizens.

author: Angie karan
text: In my perception and self - awareness of life, I see the big picture ~ I see my self ~ the place of my true home ~ the home of my soul.You are the Master of your own life - The key and beauty of your soul.

author: Dejan Stojanovic
text: There is something perfect to be found in the imperfect: the law keeps balance through the juxtaposition of beauty, which gains perfection through nurtured imperfection.

author: Dejan Stojanovic
text: Beauty is a cheap word, but beauty remains priceless.

author: Marilyn Waring
text: Men won't easily give up a system in which half the world's population works for next to nothing...[and recognizes that]precisely because that half works for so little, it may have no energy left to fight for anything else.

author: Naomi Wolf
text: In drawing attention to the physical characteristics of women leaders, they can be dismissed as either too pretty or too ugly. The net effect is to prevent women's identification with the issues. If the public women is stigmatized as too 'pretty,' she's a threat, a rival--or simply not serious; if derided as too 'ugly,' one risks tarring oneself with the same brush by identifying oneself with her agenda.

author: Everett Ruess
text: I prefer the saddle to the streetcar and star-sprinkled sky to a roof, the obscure and difficult trail leading into the unknown to any paved highway, and the deep peace of the wild to the discontent bread by cities... it is enough that I am surrounded by beauty.

author: Naomi Wolf
text: The stronger that women grow, the more prestige, fame, and money is accorded to the display professions: They are held higher and higher above the heads of rising women, for them to emulate.

author: Peggy Toney Horton
text: Ah, Lovely October, as you usher in the season that awakens my soul, your awesome beauty compels my spirit to soar like an leaf caught in an autumn breeze and my heart to sing like a heavenly choir.

author: George Sand
text: Nature alone can speak to our intelligence an imperishable language, never changing, because it remains within the bounds of eternal truth and of what is absolutely noble and beautiful.

author: Dejan Stojanovic
text: Art is apotheosis; often, the complaint of beauty.

author: Naomi Wolf
text: Aging in women is 'unbeautiful' since women grow more powerful with time, and since the links between generations of women must always be broken.

author: Naomi Wolf
text: Women have face-lifts in a society in which women without them appear to vanish from sight.

author: Naomi Wolf
text: Vogue began to focus on the body as much as on the clothes, in part because there was little they could dictate with the anarchic styles...In a stunning move, an entire replacement culture was developed by naming a 'problem' where it had scarcely existed before, centering it on the women's natural state, and elevating it to the existential female dilemma...The number of diet-related articles rose 70 percent from 1968 to 1972...The lucrative 'transfer of guilt' was resurrected just in time.

author: Naomi Wolf
text: Western women have been controlled by ideals and stereotypes as much as by material constraints.

author: Karl Pearson
text: Order and reason, beauty and benevolence, are characteristics and conceptions which we find solely associated with the mind of man.

author: Reuben Berger
text: Without Love, you can't know yourself.

author: Mahrukh
text: Walking there, she said: Look, it seems like some one has kept each stone with measured precision at its place. Yes, she was right.

author: Mahrukh
text: You do not have to run with out a sigh, sometimes you gotta stay and have a break when you breath and admire the beauty of the journey.

author: Richard Ellmann
text: Drift beautifully on the surface, and you will die unbeautifully in the depths.

author: Gollapalli Nithin Kumar
text: Truth is Bitter & It's the Real Beauty in Ugliness.

author: indonesia123
text: Sweet wine makes drunk, sour wine (insult) is "tetelestai". Life is not about what we have done and become, but how God to be fully glorified.

author: Ankit Samrat
text: Don't miss the beauty behind otherwise your whole race will end up with wasting time running on trademill.

author: Balakoteswara Panchakshari
text: Not easy, not at all for everyone to see the beauty of one's self/soul. It's all about money, nothing else.

author: Joan Ambu
text: Your beauty is yours, believe it. Do not rely on someone else to approve it.

author: Ron Brackin
text: The nature of a true seeker after beauty is to overlook flaws.

author: John Keats 1795-1821
text: Do not all charms fly / At the mere touch of cold philosophy?

author: Chuck Wachtel
text: Aim for truth, and beauty will follow. Aim for beauty, and truth will not necessarily follow.

author: Malak El Halabi
text: You have the face of a man who gently caresses field flowers and dandelions. And a smile that is like a dagger, cutting the sun in halves.

author: Rabindranath Tagore
text: Beauty is in the ideal of perfect harmony which is in the Universal Being; Truth the perfect comprehension of the Universal Mind. We individuals approach it through our own mistakes and blunders, through our accumulated experiences, through our illumined consciousness — how, otherwise, can we know Truth?

author: Jawwad Zafar
text: We crave beauty, like we crave peace.

author: Richard L.  Ratliff
text: I'd keep your beauty timeless. like a flower pressed in a book, yesI wouldn't let it fade Folded in the chapters of my mind

author: Donna Kasubeck
text: Photography saved my life by opening my eyes to the beauty that surrounds me each and everyday. Life look much richer from behind the lens.

author: Nurudeen Ushawu
text: To every corner of the planet, to the young and old, to all humanity. I see your beauty. I really do.

author: Ahlam Salhab
text: The beauty of soul is reflected by eyes

author: Akshay Vasu
text: Art is a place where tragedy meets beauty. An artist is someone who creates the most beautiful things of his life when his soul starts bleeding.

author: Swami Chetanananda
text: Through our heart, we gain access to a psychological and emotional experience of abundance that, at times for me, is overwhelming it is so beautiful. There is beauty in each of us that is truly astonishing, a beauty that expresses itself on one level as abundance and on another level as endless healing, and finally a perspective that is so peaceful, so restful, that we can reside in it even in the face of this lunatic world that we live in.

author: Lana M. H. Wilder
text: Show the world there's something to fight for. Your life is the proof that beauty can still be attained.

author: Emily St. John Mandel
text: People want what was best about the world.

author: Angie karan
text: Soulful love, is poetry in motion. A contemplation of beauty from the deep arises and the mere struggle to express the rapture of the soul.

author: Luan
text: There is an incredible beauty in your touch, it can heal the gravest wounds. And in your smile, that can easily mend any broken heart.

author: Omoakhuana Anthonia
text: A beautiful woman is one with a beautiful heart. She may be covered with mud or sores but only her foot fit the glass slipper.

author: Theodor Adorno
text: ...the beautiful in nature is like a spark flashing momentarily and disappearing as soon as one tries to get hold of it.

author: Tahar Mtibaa
text: For a man he get his own ship and his own strong wind, but he cannot stop missing all the passing breezes that never come again.

author: Angie karan
text: When your heart, mind and soul is in harmony - you walk with love, you walk with beauty.

author: Angie karan
text: When beauty is seen through the windows of the soul - rainbows appear and everything is magical. It feels simply divine.

author: Kristen Henderson
text: I wonder what became of you, your JohnnyRotten skin, no Emerald City eyes.You'd have been a beauty if you let inferiority steam your glasses with its candor, sans laughter.

author: Kristen Henderson
text: Up past the old lime kiln built into the side of a hill we take a hard right at a clearing lined by brittle apple trees still willing to bear fruit.I snap sticks beneath my feetand steal pictures of the view while you reach for something sweet, as much as it bowsto you.

author: Angie karan
text: Our inner beauty is that Kingdom of Heaven that lies within. It is a fragrance and the signature of our soul.

author: Johnathan Carter
text: one can't see beauty until one see's life the way it is

author: Vanshika Dhyani
text: What is worse losing love or never finding it at all?

author: Criss Jami
text: Perhaps not everything happens for a reason. That is, until you make it so; because for everything there is a season, which can, in fact, become beautiful.

author: Angie karan
text: The soul is everlasting. It does not change. Live from your soul essence. Dare to embrace your true, full beauty. Live in GRACE!

author: HoBs
text: Beauty becomes uglyunder the influence ofthe demons inside the mind.

author: Ricky Maye
text: Change is inevitable. Progression is a choice. We all move, but are you going to move forward?

author: Ricky Maye
text: If you do not cultivate your life's environment, you will not captivate the worlds enlightenment.

author: Ricky Maye
text: Stop looking back when your future is ahead of you

author: Maggie Nelson
text: For blue has no mind. It is not wise, nor does it promise any wisdom. It is beautiful, and despite what the poets and philosophers and theologians have said, I think beauty neither obscures truth nor reveals it. Likewise, it leads neither towards justice nor away from it. It is pharmakon. It radiates.

author: Guy de Maupassant
text: Nevertheless man has found love, which is not a bad reply to that sly Deity, and he has adorned it with so much poetry that woman often forgets the sensual part of it. Those among us who are unable to deceive themselves have invented vice and refined debauchery, which is another way of laughing at God and paying homage, immodest homage, to beauty.

author: Rabindranath Tagore
text: We cannot see Beauty till we let go our hold of it. It was Buddha who conquered the world, not Alexander - this is untrue when stated in dry prose - oh when shall we be able to sing it? When shall all these most intimate truths of the universe overflow the pages of printed books and leap out in a sacred stream like the Ganges from the Gangotrie?

author: Diana Jaber
text: Isn't it beautiful when you just stand there right in your track and watch something so amazing, so heart-warming, that you lose track of time and then don't know what to do from there onwards?

author: Goitsemang Mvula
text: There will be those who love you for your hair and those who love the beauty of your mind and those who adore the warmth of your heart. but there will be those who will leave you for not conforming to their type of hair, mind and heart. And there will be those who will live/die to see your bad hair days, derailed mind, and broken heart. but what matters most is Who You Are

author: Oksana Rus
text: Be calm...calm as a calm lagoon, then you will look beautiful as a beautiful calm lagoon crowned by the Moon and sheltered by the brilliance of the stars reclaiming your royalty of regal life...

author: Criss Jami
text: If beauty is relative, then any and everything when compared to the beauty of God is absolutely hideous.

author: Sarah Brownlee
text: The world is unbearably ugly when beauty is judged purely by what is seen on the outside.

author: Ama H. Vanniarachchy
text: Magic is seeing wonder in nature's every little thing, seeing how wonderful the fireflies are and how magical are the dragonflies.

author: Connie Kerbs
text: In the most surreal, the most joyful, the most beautiful, the most intense, the most alive moments of life, you are absorbed into the horizon which is at its most invisible, elusive, perfect blend of sky and sea.

author: MD. Muhtashimur Rahman
text: It is there as it is, not in the past, not in the future, just in the present moment. To live in the present gives a person true happiness as well as the perception of being connected to the world.

author: MD. Muhtashimur Rahman
text: True inner peace can startle you! Be happy, smile, have fun. But only look for inner peace when you actually need it. After all, it is the fusion of every atoms of reality itself.

author: Alireza Salehi Nejad
text: Seize the day and explore the allure of life.

author: Angie karan
text: Beauty is a treasure grove within. Beauty has different layers and depths. Peel and and look beyond the surface deep into the heart, the soul, and the mind

author: Socrates
text: There is one way, then, in which a man can be free from all anxiety about the fate of his soul - if in life he has abandoned bodily pleasures and adornments, as foreign to his purpose and likely to do more harm than good, and has devoted himself to the pleasures of acquiring knowledge, and so by decking his soul not with a borrowed beauty but with its own - with self-control, and goodness, and courage, and liberality, and truth - has fitted himself to await his journey in the next world.

author: L Arun
text: Beauty has its own vices.

author: Oksana Rus
text: For me, a hearty laugh is one of the most beautiful sounds in the world. It's a way of life!

author: Mary Kate
text: The beauty of a morning glory, is that of its patient wait for the sun to rise in the morning!

author: Mary Kate
text: The beauty of a morning glory, is that of its patient wait for the sun to bloom in the morning!

author: Mary Kate
text: The beauty of life isn't the perfectioned moments or storybook endings; the beauty of life is when you fall flat on your face, the Lord picks you up, then you look around and cheer, after all, a merry heart is the medicine!

author: Paul Gauguin
text: Art requires philosophy, just as philosophy requires art. Otherwise, what would become of beauty?

author: Yafreisy Carrero
text: Nature already uses the language of mathematics, so why not work with the environment instead of against it. We need to start mimicking the mathematical logic that occurs in the landscape, identify existing systems, and out of those concepts create new ones.

author: Akilnathan Logeswaran
text: Honestly, I never really understood the glorification of Fridays & weekends. I don't want to build a life and career, where I spent five days a week waiting for the weekend. No! I want to enjoy my life, and don't wish any weekday away. I want each day to matter to me, in some way, even if it's a small tiny way. I love my life. Everyday. That's the spirit we should convey all around us.

author: Mamur Mustapha
text: Beautiful moments in life need no words for description. Living those moments and feeling the beauty suffices.

author: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
text: The need for beauty and the [artistic] creation which embodies it is inseparable from man, and without it man would possibly not want to live in the world.

author: Arya vidhan
text: loneliness gives you opportunity to look the beauty of out of window

author: Manprit Kaur
text: I do not know who God is; but I have witnessed the Healing Power of Love, the Beauty of Nature, and the Wisdom of my Soul. If God can be understood in those terms, then don't you think, we all have already found the truth? I feel humanity needs to Stop Searching and Start Living the Truth. Manprit Kaur

author: Amy Carmichael
text: We profess to be strangers and pilgrims, seeking after a country of our own, yet we settle down in the most un-stranger-like fashion, exactly as if we were quite at home and meant to stay as long as we could. I don't wonder apostolic miracles have died. Apostolic living certainly has.

author: Max Lucado
text: You will never forgive anyone more than God has already forgiven you.

author: Mahatma Gandhi
text: You Christians look after a document containing enough dynamite to blow all civilisation to pieces, turn the world upside down and bring peace to a battle-torn planet. But you treat it as though it is nothing more than a piece of literature.

author: David Dark
text: What the pundits call wishy-washiness, the Bible calls repentance.

author: Charles R. Swindoll
text: Good intentions and earnest effort are not enough. Only Jesus can make an otherwise futile life productive.

author: Rolly Lavapie
text: Life in Christ is like traveling on a metro link train, with a predetermined destination. You are not the driver, Jesus is, and God provided the route on this one time trip. He plotted everything, the date and the time of your travel and arrival. There will be stops and delays along the way, but remember this, at the bottom of a traffic light is always a green light.

author: Robert McAfee Brown
text: One important aspect of justice, Jose Miranda reminds us, involves the restoration of what has been stolen. Giving food to the hungry or clothing to the naked is not a charitable handout but an exercise in simple justice - restoring to the poor what is rightfully theirs, what has been taken from them unjustly.

author: Malcolm Muggeridge
text: Christianity . . . sees the necessity for man to have spiritual values and it shows him how to get at those through physical sacraments.

author: Jen Tindugan-Adoviso
text: Of course I contradict myself. Why else would I often bite my tongue and attempt to put the fire out?

author: Anna Aquino
text: I was going to stop pretending that just because we were in ministry we were perfect. I was tired of wearing the mask of ministry, and knew that I needed to start living the life.

author: Augustine of Hippo
text: If you have understood, then what you have understood is not God.

author: Steve Cioccolanti
text: Achieving great things through training, tenacity & time doesn't make someone vain. It lessens vanity! Therefore, I have one question: is @realDonaldTrump vain?

author: Jayce O'Neal
text: We don't need to pacify our issues, we need to crucify them.

author: Kingsley Opuwari Manuel
text: Jesus is the same yesterday, today and forever and He doesn't need a makeover!

author: Meister Eckhart
text: When God laughs at the soul and the soul laughs back at God, the persons of the Trinity are begotten. When the Father laughs at the Son and the Son laughs back at the Father, that laughter gives pleasure, that pleasure gives joy, that joy gives love, and that love is the Holy Spirit.

author: Kingsley Opuwari Manuel
text: Grace is all that God is free to do for you, in you, with you and through you only because of the finished work of Jesus Christ.

author: Paul Gitwaza
text: When you are not full of the Holy Spirit, you easily cower in fear and lack a stand on truth

author: Kingsley Opuwari Manuel
text: Materialism is not having things, it is letting things have you.

author: Kellen Roggenbuck
text: If you aren't willing to fight for what you believe in, then you don't really believe in it. Faith is a verb.

author: Brandon J Brown
text: We can't understand the solutions other people arrive at until we understand the problems they are trying to solve.

author: Nadia Bolz-Weber
text: Every time I go look for God amidst sorrow, I always find Jesus at the cross, in death and resurrection. This is our God.

author: Robert Junior
text: Be good to the people on your way up the ladder cause you'll ,meet them on your way down.

author: Betsy Cornwell
text: Where once I prayed for forgiveness from a father God who held up huge palms and said “Thou shalt not,” now I find peace with a sister god who takes my open hands in hers and says, “You will.

author: Mahendra Jakhar
text: Eventually everyone dies, but death, in various forms and ways, still comes as a shock. Then they throw dirt in your face. Then the worms eat you. Or they consign you to flames. The flesh sizzles and the bones crackle. be grateful it happens in that order.

author: John Owen
text: There is no imagination wherewith man is besotted, more foolish, none so pernicious as this,- that persons not purified, not sanctified, not made holy in their life, should afterwards be taken into that state of blessedness which consists in the enjoyment of God. Neither can such persons enjoy God, nor would God be a reward to them. Holiness is perfected in heaven: but the beginning of it is invariably confined to this world.

author: J.C. Ryle
text: Hell, hell fire, the damnation of hell, eternal damnation, the resurrection of the damnation, everlasting fire, the place of torment, destruction, outer darkness, the worm that never dies, the fire that is not quenched, the place of weeping, wailing and gnashing of teeth, everlasting punishment... these are the words which the Lord Jesus Christ Himself employs. Away with the miserable nonsense which people talk in this day who tell us that the ministers of the gospel should never speak of hell.

author: Steven J. Lawson
text: The lamp of divine, written revelation reveals the will of God for the believer. Whether it is expressed by biblical command or precept, by scriptural example or principle, the Word illumines the path every believer must take. This divine light in Scripture is not a mere option, but an absolute necessity for every follower of Christ.

author: C.R. Lord
text: Man has only wisdumb to gain knowledge but God alone has wisdom, for he possesses all knowledge past, present and future and there is not one iota of knowledge that he does not possess or will not possess.

author: Sheila Walsh
text: ...I believe that doubts, honestly expressed and wrestled with, produce a faith that is stronger and more intimate than doubts suppressed under the veneer of faith.

author: Steven Chuks Nwaokeke
text: Refusal to engage in spiritual warfare does not exempt you from being among the next casualties of war

author: Becky Watson
text: Human nature is never satisfied.

author: Charles Haddon Spurgeon
text: A true prayer is an inventory of needs, a catalog of necessities, an exposure of secret wounds, a revelation of hidden poverty.

author: J.C. Ryle
text: We live in a day of abounding vagueness and indistinctness on doctrinal subjects in religion. Now, if ever, it is the duty of all advocates of clear, well-defined, sharply-cut theology, to supply proof that their views are thoroughly borne out by Scripture.

author: J.C. Ryle
text: Ignorance of Scripture is the root of every error in religion, and the source of ever heresy. To be allowed to remove a few grains of ignorance, and to throw a few rays of light on God's precious word, is, in my opinion, the greatest honor that can be put on a Christian.

author: Nehemiah Rogers
text: Zeal, if it be well ordered, is most beautiful in a Christian; but if not, it is a thing of exceeding great danger: as fire in moderation is most comfortable, but in extremity most fearful.

author: Sheldon Vanauken
text: Her death...brought me as nothing else could do to know and end my jealousy of God. It saved her faith from assault.

author: Joseph Alleine
text: In every sound convert the judgement is brought to approve of the laws and ways of Christ, and subscribe to them as most righteous and reasonable; the desire of the heart is to know the whole mind of Christ; the free and resolved choice of the heart is determined for the ways of Christ, before all the pleasures of sin, and prosperities of the world; it is the daily care of his life to walk with God.

author: Undena Y. Leake Jackson
text: Let's take off the masks and get real so we can get it right with God.

author: James Denney

text: As humanity perfects itself, man becomes degraded. When everything is reduced to the mere counter-balancing of economic interests, what room will there be for virtue? When Nature has been so subjugated that she has lost all her original forms, where will that leave the plastic arts? And so on. In the mean time, things are going to get very murky.

author: Max Ernst
text: When the artist finds himself he is lost. The fact that he has succeeded in never finding himself is regarded by Max Ernst as his only lasting achievement.

author: Virginia Woolf
text: It was a miserable machine, an inefficient machine, she thought, the human apparatus for painting or for feeling; it always broke down at the critical moment; heroically, one must force it on.

author: Benjamin West
text: Remember, light and shadow never stand still.

author: Andrew Davidson
text: The urge is always with me to retouch yesterday's canvas with today's paintbrush and cover the things that fill me with regret..

author: Ben-Hur: A Tale of the Christ
text: The architect had not stopped to bother about columns and porticos, proportions or interiors, or any limitation upon the epic he sought to materialize; he had simply made a servant of Nature - art can go no further.

author: Oscar Wilde
text: I regard the theatre as the greatest of all art forms, the most immediate way in which a human being can share with another the sense of what it is to be a human being.

author: Edward Hopper
text: No amount of skillful invention can replace the essential element of imagination.

author: Mike  Norton
text: Mastering the art of seduction gives one a great power, and like any power, it's to be wielded with responsibility; a man who wields the art of seduction without a sense of responsibility and restraint is a walking proximity bomb of viral epidemics, needless procreation, heartbroken families, and shattered dreams.

author: Rebecca McNutt
text: Nobody has ever taken a photograph of something they want to forget. We can build a wall of happy Kodak moments around ourselves, a wall of our Christmases, birthdays, baby showers and weddings, but we can never forget that celluloid film is see-through, that behind it, all the misery of real life waits for our wall to collapse someday.

author: André Breton
text: (speaking of Ann Radcliffe) A work of art worthy of the name is one which gives us back the freshness of the emotions of childhood.

author: Jackson Pollock
text: every good artist paints what he is

author: Artur Schnabel
text: The notes I handle no better than many pianists. But the pauses between the notes - ah, that is where the art resides.

author: Joanna Russ
text: Minority art, vernacular art, is marginal art. Only on the margins does growth occur.

author: Jasper Johns
text: My experience with life is that it's very fragmented. In one place certain kinds of thing occur, and in another place a different kind of thing occurs. I would like my work to have some vivid indication of those differences. I guess, in painting, it would amount to different kinds of space being represented in it.

author: Marc Chagall
text: Color is all. When color is right, form is right. Color is everything, color is vibration like music; everything is vibration.

author: Hiroko Sakai
text: When you want to make the main color pure and bright, don't just keep adding bright colors on it. Just make the colors around the spot darker and dull. It will give the scene dramatical effects.I think the life is the same.

author: Julian Barnes
text: He thought of trying to explain something he had recently noticed about himself: that if anyone insulted him, or one of his friends, he didn't really mind--or not much, anyway. Whereas if anyone insulted a novel, a story, a poem that he loved, something visceral and volcanic occurred within him. He wasn't sure what this might mean--except perhaps that he had got life and art mixed up, back to front, upside down.

author: Andy Goldsworthy
text: My art is an attempt to reach beyond the surface appearance. I want to see growth in wood, time in stone, nature in a city, and I do not mean its parks but a deeper understanding that a city is nature too-the ground upon which it is built, the stone with which it is made.

author: Lana Del Rey
text: Like a groupie incognito posing as a real singer, life imitates art.

author: Dejan Stojanovic
text: Perfection seems sterile; it is final, no mystery in it; it's a product of an assembly line.

author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
text: Colors are light's suffering and joy

author: Paul Gauguin
text: Color which, like music, is a matter of vibrations, reaches what is most general and therefore most indefinable in nature: its inner power.

author: Ron Hall
text: Art teaches something we all need to learn, especially about people who are different from ourselves: "To see things the way they truly are, sometimes you have to look more deeply.

author: Tyree Guyton
text: Life itself is an art form.

author: Hermann Bahr
text: It comforted him because it could not be called suffering if it was a sign of Art.

author: Jean Rousset
text: Art’s only concern with the real is to abolish it, and to substitute for it a new reality

author: Dejan Stojanovic
text: In trying to be perfect, He perfected the art of anonymity, Became imperceptible And arrived nowhere from nowhere.

author: Marc Chagall
text: In the arts, as in life, everything is possible provided it is based on love.

author: Paul Klee
text: Color has got me. I no longer need to chase after it. It has got me for ever. I know it. That is the meaning of this happy hour.

author: Iimani David
text: Art cannot be bought or sold. It can only be created or destroyed.

author: Ruadhán J. McElroy
text: Nothing is new anymore. We're living in a post-everything society and "art" itself has become satire.

author: Danny De Vito
text: It's fun to be on the edge. I think you do your best work when you take chances when you're not safe when you're not in the middle of the road...

author: Albrecht Dürer
text: Truly, art is embedded in nature; he who can extract it, has it.

author: Dejan Stojanovic
text: We love the imperfect shapes in nature and in the works of art, look for an intentional error as a sign of the golden key and sincerity found in true mastery.

author: Dejan Stojanovic
text: Sound unbound by nature becomes bounded by art.

author: Olivia Sinaga
text: Art is my Life.

author: Tom Dolby
text: But maybe that's how it is with art. You suffer, and in the end, everyone thinks it's cool.

author: Robert Rauschenberg
text: Painting relates to both art and life. Neither can be made - I try to act in the gap.

author: Theodore J. Kaczynski
text: Art forms that appeal to [leftists] tend to focus on ... defeat and despair ... as if there were no hope of accomplishing anything through rational calculation.

author: Vesa Peltonen
text: there is no problems, only solutions".

author: Iimani David
text: The market follows the artist. The artist does not follow the market.

author: Jackson Pollock
text: The painting has a life of its own

author: Darnell Lamont Walker
text: The scary part of being an artist is knowing that what makes you a better artist can also kill you.

author: Christian Bobin
text: Nothing is owed to us in life, not even the innocence of a blue sky. Great art is the art of thankfulness for the abundance of every moment. Writing is a Chinese variant of this thankfulness, a courtesy to life in its cloak of nothing, lined with love.

author: Marty Johncox
text: It's true that a picture is worth a thousand words, but it's also true that a word is worth a thousand pictures.

author: Lucifer
text: For a pregnant woman to give birth, she's gotta feel the pain of pulling a watermelon out of her nostril. For an Artist to create a masterpiece, he's gotta feel the pain of pulling entire galaxies out of his ass.

author: Diego Rivera
text: An artist is above all a human being, profoundly human to the core. If the artist can’t feel everything that humanity feels, if the artist isn’tcapable of loving until he forgets himself and sacrifices himself if necessary, if he won’t put down his magic brush and head the fightagainst the oppressor, then he isn’t a great artist.

author: Lepota L. Cosmo
text: Facts produce structures, objects are lyrical realities.

author: P.H. Wilson
text: When you speak of my insanity, please let it be with the beauty only art knows. Let it bleed till it becomes creativity and maybe, just maybe, for that single moment my soul will finally be adorned in its own skin.

author: Michelle C. Hillstrom
text: Pain fuels artistry and creativity. Harness your suffering and become a master of your art.

author: Tupac Shakur
text: If we really are saying rap is an art form, then we got to be more responsible for our lyrics. If you see everybody dying because of what you saying, it don’t matter that you didn’t make them die, it just matters that you didn’t save them.

author: Dagara Tribe Member
text: You are my other self

author: Edward Tufte
text: We shouldn’t abbreviate the truth but rather get a new method of presentation.

author: Marwa A.A
text: Life is an art the one cannot erase

author: Valdas Partee
text: When life, inspiration, and pen meet.

author: Ron Brackin
text: It is not sufficient for artistic expressions to serve as "signposts declaring what it is to be fully human." They should impart a vision of what it can be to become divine.

author: Efrat Cybulkiewicz
text: Art fuels the fire inside me.

author: Efrat Cybulkiewicz
text: My response to stress is just as complex as my artwork.

author: Gabor Gürtler
text: I believe, that creating is a joyful activity as well as a meaningful suffer, and thus, it is an integral part of the human nature.

author: C.S. Lewis
text: The knight is a man of blood and iron, a man familiar with the sight of smashed faces and the ragged stumps of lopped-off limbs; he is also a demure, almost maidenlike, guest in a hall, a gentle, modest, unobtrusive man. He is not compromise or happy mean between ferocity and meekness; he is fierce to the nth and meek to the nth. The man who combines both characters – the knight – is not a work of nature but of art; of that art which has human beings, instead of canvas or marble, for its medium.

author: Bruce Lee
text: True mastery transcends any particular art. It stems from mastery of oneself--the ability, developed through self-discipline, to be calm, fully aware, and completely in tune with oneself and the surroundings. Then, and only then, can a person know himself.

author: Tracy Weinzapfel
text: Life is the art of drawing without an eraser.

author: Tristan Tzara
text: I am writing a manifesto and there's nothing I want, and yet I'm saying certain things, and in principle I am against manifestos, as I am against principles.

author: kevin mcpherson eckhoff
text: The notion of "cause and effect" is sometimes useful in real life, and it can even be interesting in art, but I'm more interested in "cause and cause" or "effect and effect" or "and and and".

author: Kowtham Kumar K
text: I often come across this question. "Which is the best camera in the world?". I would always say, "Well. You already own two of it, since your birth.

author: Gerald Mills
text: This mind is continuous and ever taxing, Sleep is an endeavoring luxury for the carnivorous mind

author: Tim Mann artist
text: Don’t fear the future or regret the past but celebrate the present.

author: Tim Mann artist
text: Every human is unique every spirit is engaging.

author: Mark Rothko
text: You’ve got sadness in you, I’ve got sadness in me – and my works of art are places where the two sadnesses can meet, and therefore both of us need to feel less sad.

author: Pradeepa Pandiyan
text: Not every artistic person should have to be a photographer, but every photographer should be artistic.

author: douglas m laurent
text: linear brains can't curve a thought.

author: Ai Weiwei
text: We are living in a very complex society. It puts me in a complex frame of thinking.

author: Ellen Forney
text: Sometimes it seems like "pain" is too obvious a place to turn for inspiration. Pain isn't always deep, anyway. Sometimes it's awful and that's it. Or boring. Surely other things can be as profound as pain.

author: Sotero M Lopez II
text: When you master the art of work, then your life becomes a work of art...and you're the artist and no one else paints your life for you.

author: Kurt Vonnegut Jr.
text: The primary benefit of practicing any art, whether well or badly, is that it enables one's soul to grow.

author: Elle Luna
text: I believe that when you step into uncharted territory, you are also stepping into total abandonment, potential humiliation, and a space where nothing is guaranteed; there’s no case study or roadmap. I have so much respect for anybody who will step away from what they can do in order to find what they must do. That’s a hallmark characteristic of entrepreneurs and artists. And it’s scary and exciting as all hell.

author: Piet Mondrian
text: I wish to approach truth as closely as is possible, and therefore I abstract everything until I arrive at the fundamental quality of objects.

author: Criss Jami
text: In the heart of appeasement there's the fear of rejection, and in acts of fear there are mirrors of oppression.

author: Armin Houman
text: Art is not about achievement, but rather a new perspective to look from.

author: Ayn Rand
text: An artist reveals his naked soul in his work - and so, gentle reader, do you when you respond to it.

author: Sondra Faye
text: Some of the greatest masterpieces of art are created against the odds of reality.from the book: stuff i think about

author: Czesław Miłosz
text: Horror is the law of the world of living creatures, and civilization is concerned with masking that truth. Literature and art refine and beautify, and if they were to depict reality naked, just as everyone suspects it is (although we defend ourselves against that knowledge), no one would be able to stand it.

author: Micheline Jean Louis
text: Allow the courage to create overwhelmed you.

author: Dorothy L. Sayers
text: That a work of creation struggles and insistently demands to be brought into being is a fact that no genuine artist would think of denying.

author: J.R. Stewart
text: Some things are meant to live and die with an artist

author: Lawrence Durrell
text: I don’t believe one reads to escape reality. A person reads to confirm a reality he knows is there, but which he has not experienced.

author: Isaac Asimov
text: Congratulations on the new library, because it isn't just a library. It is a space ship that will take you to the farthest reaches of the Universe, a time machine that will take you to the far past and the far future, a teacher that knows more than any human being, a friend that will amuse you and console you -- and most of all, a gateway, to a better and happier and more useful

author: Mark Vonnegut
text: What occurs to people when they read Kurt [Vonnegut] is that things are much more up for grabs than they thought they were. The world is a slightly different place just because they read a damn book. Imagine that.

author: M.H. Abrams
text: We are human, and nothing is more interesting to us than humanity. The appeal of literature is that it is so thoroughly a human thing — by, for and about human beings. If you lose that focus, you obviate the source of the power and permanence of literature.

author: W.H. Auden
text: To read is to translate, for no two persons' experiences are the same. A bad reader is like a bad translator: he interprets literally when he ought to paraphrase and paraphrases when he ought to interpret literally.

author: Angie Thomas
text: One of my biggest influences as a writer is J. K. Rowling. I grew up with Harry Potter. One thing I absolutely loved was how every single person in Harry's world was so three-dimensional—it was as if each one was the main character in his or her own story and was just making a guest appearance in Harry's story. I strive to do that as a writer. I want every side character to be the main character of his or her own story.

author: Will Advise
text: What's writ is what's read, yet the meaning is gone, since context is what gives each quote its own home.

author: McKenna Pickett
text: Reading is an escape people use in order to get away from reality. It is a chance to be free and explore who you are.

author: Max Lerner
text: The crime of book purging is that it involves a rejection of the word. For the word is never absolute truth, but only man’s frail and human effort to approach the truth. To reject the word is to reject the human search.

author: Charles Baxter
text: Everybody should read something. Otherwise we all fall down into the pit of ignorance. Many are down there. Some people fall in it forever. Their lives mean nothing. They should not exist. (From the short story, "Charity".)

author: Jade
text: Words will change your future

author: David Hill
text: How can I survive without a book to read?

author: JennAnijah Publishing
text: Because What we Learn from our Favorite Books, you see in our daily Lives.---JennAnijah Publishing

author: Elena Ferrante
text: ...but I was bored, I could scarcely understand them. I started to borrow novels from the circulating library, and read one after the other. But in the long run they didn't help. They presented intense lives, profound conversations, a phantom reality more appealing than my real life. So, in order to feel as if I were not real, I sometimes went...

author: Gautama Buddha
text: Peace comes from within.  Do not seek it without.

author: Elizabeth Gilbert
text: Imagine that the universe is a great spinning engine. You want to stay near the core of the thing - right in the hub of the wheel - not out at the edges where all the wild whirling takes place, where you can get frayed and crazy. The hub of calmness - that's your heart. That's where God lives within you. So stop looking for answers in the world. Just keep coming back to that center and you'll always find peace.

author: Dalai Lama XIV
text: When we feel love and kindness toward others, it not only makes others feel loved and cared for, but it helps us also to develop inner happiness and peace.

author: Pablo Neruda
text: I move in the university of the waves.

author: Gary Markwick
text: Once you can let go of illusion and draw upon a more universal source of motivation then you will re connect with your true purpose on Earth.

author: V.S. Atbay
text: Let the wet earth embrace you firmly, soundly. She needs to be revived, she needs to beat like a heart full of adrenaline inside a chest.

author: Muhaya Haji Mohamad
text: The NOW is such a magical moment that you have the time to live a magical life and have no time to have guilt of the past, worry of the future but to live now fully and unfold our magnificence with the help of Allah

author: Jennifer White
text: The more we try to control the things outside of us the more we lose control of our mind.

author: Rousseau Jean-Jacques 1712-1778
text: The body should be strong enough to obey the mind; a good servant must be strong. I know that intemperance stimulates the passions; in course of time it also destroys the body; fasting and penance often produce the same results in an opposite way. The weaker the body, the more imperious its demands; the stronger it is, the better it obeys. All sensual passions find their home in effeminate bodies; the less satisfaction they can get the keener their sting.

author: Renae A.Sauter
text: No one knows while experiencing their darkest hour that some day they may use that very experience to illuminate the ways for others. Nothing is ever wasted.

author: Parna Chowdhury
text: Tides washed the wounds but the scars remained and continued to burn whenever a similar wind blew...

author: Maryum Ahsam
text: Prayer is the best way to face any problem, to crush every fear and to release every pain

author: Adam Oakley
text: Sometimes you just have to turn off the lights, sit in the dark, and see what happens inside of you.

author: Rajasaraswathii
text: I am neither the mind not the thought, I am its Creator.

author: Erin Fal Haskell
text: To the extent to which your consciousness is limited or expanded, is the extent to which you experience being divided or divine.

author: Arthur Schopenhauer
text: There is an underlying unity in all things

author: Alaric Hutchinson
text: Conflict forces us to be fully present because it shatters our ego – stripping away all hope of escape or sugar coating. It removes everything that is nonessential to our authentic being; it removes all superficial layers. Conflict is painful because it wakes us up out of our created illusions. And if we lean into it, conflict can be the catalyst to our enlightenment.

author: Alaric Hutchinson
text: Your sweet-toting and sugarcoating is of no service to anyone! Do not sugarcoat reality; it only gives the people in your life a sweet-tooth that then makes it more challenging for them to later bite down on the hardness of life. Do not tote and tout sweets either – you’re malnourishing people! Instead give them the truth. What is the truth you may ask? Authentic expression of who you really are, how you really feel, without projecting the labels of right or wrong.

author: Gabriel Brunsdon
text: The science of the spirit and its relationship to the body in which it indwells is a complex conundrum. Life is not what it appears to be. Life is wholesome, and this unison of synergistic amalgamations persuade the common view that one thing is the other. But one thing is many things - at the one time - and this simple truth goes to the essence of all life with its manifold complexities.

author: Alaric Hutchinson
text: We do not want to deny existence. Yet we also do not want to limit existence. Thus, we observe and honor without forming opinion, labeling, or adding a story to the object of our observation.

author: Summerlyn Guthrie
text: WE GROW IN SPIRIT WITH EACH LESSONLEARNED THROUGHEXPERIENCE...LET US BE THANKFULNO MATTER HOW PAINFULTHE LESSON!!!

author: Criss Jami
text: There are those who feel that the world is ultimately moving closer to Truth and to prosperity as the times evolve; then there are those who feel that it is ultimately moving farther away from Truth and into self-destruction. From this, and if it were really that simplistic, one might get the impression that life gravitates slightly into two types of people whom which are diametrically opposed in spirit.

author: Alaric Hutchinson
text: Are you able to remain humble and kind when things do not go the way you want or expect? Be kind when you are in pain; be kind even when your life seems to be falling apart around you. Be humble not only when you succeed but also when you fail. Kindness in word and action, and humble in thought and belief. It is important to not only say and do the ‘right’ thing, it is important to also think and believe it - which is being genuine in nature of peace embodiment.

author: Paracelsus
text: There is an earthly sun, which is the cause of all heat, and all who are able to see may see the sun; and those who are blind and cannot see him may feel his heat. There is an Eternal Sun, which is the source of all wisdom, and those whose spiritual senses have awakened to life will see that sun and be conscious of His existence; but those who have not attained spiritual consciousness may yet feel His power by an inner faculty which is called Intuition.

author: Iman Ghavamabadi
text: Seeing is an art; To become an artist, you need to feel.

author: Sépi
text: It is not so much being all that you dream of becoming as it is un-becoming all that is covering your being.

author: Sépi
text: It is not so much being all that we dream of becoming as it is un-becoming all that is covering our being.

author: Saim Cheeda
text: Where there is darkness, there once was light.

author: Tehya Sky
text: Through me, I see you. Through you, I see me.

author: Tehya Sky
text: The odds are stacked against us until we realize: We make the odds.

author: Marie Curie
text: Be less curious about people and more curious about ideas.

author: Victor Hugo
text: Reason is intelligence taking exercise. Imagination is intelligence with an erection.

author: Walter Lippmann
text: Where all think alike, no one thinks very much.

author: Lyman Bryson
text: The error of youth is to believe that intelligence is a substitute for experience, while the error of age is to believe experience is a substitute for intelligence.

author: Frans de Waal
text: If we look straight and deep into a chimpanzee's eyes, an intelligent self-assured personality looks back at us. If they are animals, what must we be?

author: George Scialabba
text: Perhaps imagination is only intelligence having fun.

author: Louis Zukofsky
text: Infinite is a meaningless word: except – it states / The mind is capable of performing / an endless process of addition.

author: AainaA-Ridtz
text: A positive needs a negative to complete its cycle, as the Moon needs an embodiment of itself, the Sun, to complete the cycle of its illusory essence, the Earth. Now if the earth is in dire straits, is bombing the moon to discover whether water is ‘perceived’ in the natural stance of humans an intelligent move?

author: Daniel Marques
text: Some people get offended by what I write, by what I do with my life and by what I say to those they never saw. And they also get offended when told they are too stupid to have the right to judge anyone. These poor souls don't know that respect and intelligence are correlated.

author: David Lynch
text: I look at the world and I see absurdity all around me. People do strange things constantly, to the point that, for the most part, we manage not to see it.

author: Retin Obasohan
text: Sight is seeing what's there, vision is seeing what's possible

author: Magnus Nwagu Amudi
text: The most intelligent or brilliant of us all are not usually the most successful, financially or career wise.A lot depends on the ability of a person to break into circles, meet people, network and interact.A well marketed yam may sell better than a not-so-well marketed Jollof.Do not just stay in the library and read all the books there, lest you become publicly dusty like the books you read.Food for thought!

author: Angie karan
text: Are you eating to live or are you eating to die? Food is not just for nourishment. Food is for information, it is for intelligence. It is for wisdom, but more so it is to create clarity within your self.

author: James Emlund
text: Life is a solvent. Be someone who dispels or weakens attitudes and situations. Have assets in excess to protect your liabilities. Solving it by shutting away differences in intelligence means you fail at the ultimate test. How we recognize words, how one uses words to communicate, and the ability to receive and contemplate outcomes. This is a feature (as far as we know) unique to our sort of intelligence.

author: Christopher Langan
text: There’s no logical connection between being smart and having money.

author: Michael Smith
text: You cannot control life, but you can change the way you see life.Animals other than man are more fulfilled, because they have less mind blocking life, but they are stuck with the perspective and perception they are born with. We (human beings) can greatly improve our perception by learning the ultimate truth.All the problems we have stem from people not knowing the truth of life.

author: Rebecca McNutt
text: These days we have Smartphones, Smartcars, Smartboards, Smarteverything, but consider this: if technology is getting smarter, does that mean humans are getting dumber?

author: Jack Chalker
text: An intelligent man [doesn’t] know everything, he simply [knows] how to look everything up quickly and efficiently." - Jack Chalker, Songs of the Dancing Gods

author: Md. Mujib Ullah
text: An intelligent person positively accepts criticism, repeatedly thinks before giving any statement, and is capable of motivating himself/herself to be successful in the terrible situations in the way of life journey.

author: Elon Musk
text: I think it’s important to reason from first principles rather than by analogy. The normal way we conduct our lives is we reason by analogy. [With analogy] we are doing this because it’s like something else that was done, or it is like what other people are doing. [With first principles] you boil things down to the most fundamental truths…and then reason up from there.

author: Hasse Jerner
text: Facts and science without the presence of wisdom and reason are worth a little less than nothing, while wisdom and reason without the presence of facts and science are worth far more than people without wisdom and reason are capable to expect.

author: Prabakaran Thirumalai
text: Knowledge is all about knowing it and Intelligence is all about using it

author: Marcel Proust
text: Just is not by other men of intelligence that an intelligent an is afraid of being thought a fool, so it is not by the great gentleman but by boors and 'bounders' that a man of fashion is afraid of finding his social value underrated. Three-fourths of the mental ingenuity displayed, of the social falsehoods scattered broadcast ever since the world began by people whose importance they have served only to diminish, have been aimed at inferiors.

author: Robert A. Heinlein
text: If God meant for people to fly, He would have given them brains.

author: Thomas Henry Huxley
text: Try to learn something about everything and everything about something.

author: Anderson Cooper
text: The tide of history only advances when people make themselves fully visible.

author: Gustave Flaubert
text: From time to time, I open a newspaper. Things seem to be proceeding at a dizzying rate. We are dancing not on the edge of a volcano, but on the wooden seat of a latrine, and it seems to me more than a touch rotten. Soon society will go plummeting down and drown in nineteen centuries of shit. There’ll be quite a lot of shouting. (1850)

author: Hannah Arendt
text: Forgiveness is the only way to reverse the irreversible flow of history.

author: Nico Robin
text: Fools who don't respect the past are doomed to repeat it.

author: William Morton
text: There's no crying in the rank book.

author: Shimon Peres
text: We should use our imagination more than our memory.

author: George Orwell
text: What can the England of 1940 have in common with the England of 1840? But then, what have you in common with the child of five whose photograph your mother keeps on the mantelpiece? Nothing, except that you happen to be the same person.

author: Vasily Grossman
text: There is a deep and undeniable sadness in all this: whenever we see the dawn of an eternal good that will never be overcome by evil – an evil that is itself eternal but will never succeed in overcoming good – whenever we see this dawn, the blood of old people and children is always shed.

author: Thorbjørn Jagland

author: Dejan Stojanovic

author: Boris Pasternak

author: Daniel Nayeri

author: Herodotus
text: Now if a man thus favoured died as he has lived, he will be just the one you are looking for: the only sort of person who deserves to be called happy. But mark this: until he is dead, keep the word "happy" in reserve. Till then, he is not happy, but only lucky...

author: C. N. Lester
text: We assume that anything that is new to us is new to human society as a whole, and that if we don’t see it reflected in history textbooks and in recent memory then it cannot have existed for long.

author: Mamur Mustapha
text: A religion deeply rooted in theology, is never above skepticism hinged upon the twin pillars; of reason & facts.

author: Rhian J. Martin
text: There was a certain untamed energy about the west of Ireland – full of tragedy and struggle, sown with the flesh of the departed.

author: Nico J. Genes

author: ETC Wanyanwu
text: History will only remember those that remembered it and the best way to make history is to read history

author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
text: All things are engaged in writing their history...Not a foot steps into the snow, or along the ground, but prints in characters more or less lasting, a map of its march. The ground is all memoranda and signatures; and every object covered over with hints. In nature, this self-registration is incessant, and the narrative is the print of the seal.

author: C. J. Sansom
text: However much one lacks piety, the atmosphere in a graveyard encourages quiet reflection.

author: Pradeepa Pandiyan
text: It is OK if you don't fit in, history only remembers the exceptional.

author: Sandeep N Tripathi
text: Moment by moment, in life's winter life frozeEchoing a history of blues, a milestone rose

author: Marco Tulliio Cicerone
text: To be ignorant of what occurred before you were born is to remain always a child. For what is the worth of human life, unless it is woven into the life of ancestors' by the records of history?

author: Robert Wesley Miller
text: ITS nomimal without all on transfer of regard, that weight of a measure of lines cannot be equal in comparison. The want of privacy is a need of personality not character. Only through devotional love not modernity can you coolect the past, present and future. Timeless is not what you think or hear. Patience is not any big reveal. Never see make how all free?

author: Christopher L. Bennett
text: The best we can do is take the history we have and deal with it.

author: Laurence Overmire
text: Those who oppose equality, compassion and social justice have been on the wrong side of history time and time again.

author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
text: The history of my life is the history of the struggle between an overwhelming urge to write and a combination of circumstances bent on keeping me from it.

author: Leo Tolstoy
text: Instead of the former divinely appointed aims of the Jewish, Greek, or Roman nations, which ancient historians regarded as representing the progress of humanity, modern history has postulated its own aims- the welfare of the French, German, or English people, or, in its highest abstraction, the welfare and civilization of humanity in general, by which is usually meant that of the peoples occupying a small northwesterly portion of a large continent.

author: Karl Marx
text: History is not like some individual person, which uses men to achieve its ends. History is nothing but the actions of men in pursuit of their ends.

author: R.M. Donaldson
text: Ignoring the evils of our history will only cause them to reoccur.

author: Vera Brittain
text: The fact that, within ten years, I lost one world, and after a time rose again, as it were, from spiritual death to find another, seems to me one of the strongest arguments against suicide that life can provide. There may not be - I believe that there is not - resurrection after death, but nothing could prove more conclusively than my own brief but eventful history the fact that resurrection is possible within our limited span of earthly time.

author: Arthur Herman
text: To fall for the notion of a 'double truth' and argue there was one set of truths for reason and another for faith and never the two shall meet made nonsense of the idea of truth itself.

author: Vanzetti
text: I sought my liberty and the liberty of all, my happiness and the happiness of all. I wanted a roof for every family, bread for every mouth, education for every heart, light for every intellect. I am convinced that human history has not yet begun, that we find ourselves in the last period of the prehistoric. I see with the eyes of my soul how the sky is diffused with the rays of the new millennium.

author: Star Wars: The Force Awakens
text: If you live long enough, you see the same eyes in different people

author: Tomichan Matheikal
text: History is replete with blunders written by sycophants.

author: Dr. Ron Harris
text: Those who have chosen to provide for the health and well being of others. Call them homoeopaths, allopaths and whatever one may, they must remember, they have been called and have chosen to serve. Dr. Ron Harris - 1965

author: Dr. Ron Harris
text: The world we have created has problems, that can be resolved by rich getting richer, bu by sharing we can. Ron Harris - 2008

author: Mamur Mustapha
text: History has always been violent, unstoppable and bound to happen; either with or without you. Acknowledge it.

author: M.T. Bass
text: While victors may get to write history, novelists get to write/right reality.

author: Michael Bronski
text: I have come to realize that in life and politics, there is always more to take into consideration.

author: Federico García Lorca
text: Look at the longing, the anguish of a sad fossil world / that cannot find the accent of its first sob.

author: Adolf Hitler
text: It's possible to satisfy the needs of the inner life by an intimate communion with nature, or by knowledge of the past.

author: Tony Judt
text: The historian’s task is not to disrupt for the sake of it, but it is to tell what is almost always an uncomfortable story and explain why the discomfort is part of the truth we need to live well and live properly. A well organized society is one in which we know the truth about ourselves collectively, not one in which we tell pleasant lies about ourselves.

author: Jane Addams
text: The good we secure for ourselves is precarious and uncertain until it is secured for all of us and incorporated into our common life.

author: Anne Frank

author: Ellen DeGeneres

author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
text: People do not seem to realise that their opinion of the world is also a confession of their character.

author: George Bernard Shaw
text: A Native American elder once described his own inner struggles in this manner: Inside of me there are two dogs. One of the dogs is mean and evil. The other dog is good. The mean dog fights the good dog all the time. When asked which dog wins, he reflected for a moment and replied, The one I feed the most.

author: Anaïs Nin
text: Each contact with a human being is so rare, so precious, one should preserve it.

author: Andy Rooney

author: Abigail Adams
text: I hate to complain...No one is without difficulties, whether in high or low life, and every person knows best where their own shoe pinches.

author: Steven Moffat

Nothing can stop it, nothing. Until one tiny, damp little island says "No. No, not here." A mouse in front of a lion. You're amazing, the lot of you. I don't know what you do to Hitler, but you frighten the hell out of me.

text: Who would deduce the dragonfly from the larva, the iris from the bud, the lawyer from the infant? ...We are all shape-shifters and magical reinventors. Life is really a plural noun, a caravan of selves.

author: Jacques-Yves Cousteau
text: Water and air, the two essential fluids on which all life depends, have become global garbage cans.

author: Adolf Hitler
text: As in everything, nature is the best instructor.

author: Samuel Butler
text: Autumn is the mellower season, and what we lose in flowers we more than gain in fruits.

author: Frank Lloyd Wright
text: Nature is my manifestation of God. I go to nature every day for inspiration in the day's work.

author: Leo Tolstoy
text: One can no more approach people without love than one can approach bees without care. Such is the quality of bees...

author: Sherwood Smith
text: The only noise now was the rain, pattering softly with the magnificent indifference of nature for the tangled passions of humans.

author: Jacques-Yves Cousteau
text: For most of history, man has had to fight nature to survive; in this century he is beginning to realize that, in order to survive, he must protect it.

author: Leonardo da Vinci
text: Water is the driving force in nature.

author: Lorraine Anderson
text: Nature has been for me, for as long as I remember, a source of solace, inspiration, adventure, and delight; a home, a teacher, a companion.

author: Mercedes Lackey
text: This I think I have learned: where there is love, the form does not matter, and the gods are pleased. This I have observed: what occurs in nature, comes by the hand of nature, and if the gods did not approve, it would not be there~ Moondance k'Treva (Magic's Pawn)

author: John Muir
text: There is a love of wild nature in everybody, an ancient mother-love showing itself whether recognized or no, and however covered by cares and duties

author: Edward Abbey
text: The love of wilderness is more than a hunger for what is always beyong reach; it is also an expression of loyalty to the earth, the earth which bore us and sustains us, the only paradise we shall ever know, the only paradise we ever need, if only we had the eyes to see.

author: Henry Miller
text: The world is not to be put in order. The world is order. It is for us to put ourselves in unison with this order.

author: Ivan Turgenev
text: Nature cares nothing for logic, our human logic: she has her own, which we do not recognize and do not acknowledge until we are crushed under its wheel.

author: Scott Westerfeld
text: It’s amazing how quickly nature consumes human places after we turn our backs on them. Life is a hungry thing.

author: John Keats
text: Scenery is fine -but human nature is finer

author: Supriya Kaur Dhaliwal
text: To watch the dawn emerge from the night undoubtedly gives a heavenly feeling! The fresh sun rays entwine with the dark horizon and peep out of the creek with tranquil grin.

author: Wallace Stevens
text: I know noble accentsAnd lucid, inescapable rhythms;But I know, too,That the blackbird is involvedIn what I know.

author: Wendell Berry
text: I believe until fairly recently our destructions of nature were more or less unwitting -- the by-products, so to speak, of our ignorance or weakness or depravity. It is our present principled and elaborately rationalized rape and plunder of the natural world that is a new thing under the sun.

author: Robert Browning
text: Days decrease, / And autumn grows, autumn in everything.

author: Ruskin Bond
text: ...for everytime I see the sky I'm aware of belonging to the universe than to just one corner of the earth.

author: H.G. Wells
text: The study of Nature makes a man at last as remorseless as Nature.

author: Antoni Gaudí
text: Nothing is invented, for it's written in nature first.

author: Aldous Huxley
text: My father considered a walk among the mountains as the equivalent of churchgoing.

author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
text: Nature is a language and every new fact one learns is a new word; but it is not a language taken to pieces and dead in the dictionary, but the language put together into a most significant and universal sense. I wish to learn this language--not that I may know a new grammar, but that I may read the great book which is written in that tongue.

author: Marco Pierre White
text: A tree without roots is just a piece of wood.

author: Katharine Graham
text: A mistake is simply another way of doing things.

author: David Brower
text: The wild places are where we began. When they end, so do we.

author: Kurt Vonnegut Jr.
text: If people think nature is their friend then they sure don't need an enemy.

author: Charles Baudelaire
text: Nature is a temple in which living columns sometimes emit confused words. Man approaches it through forests of symbols, which observe him with familiar glances.

author: Ningraj
text: You can predict anything in this world but not the nature's behaviour

author: John Masefield
text: Only the road and the dawn, the sun, the wind, and the rain,And the watch fire under stars, and sleep, and the road again.

author: Tomson Highway
text: English is so hierarchical. In Cree, we don't have animate-inanimate comparisons between things. Animals have souls that are equal to ours. Rocks have souls, trees have souls. Trees are 'who,' not 'what.

author: Francis Bacon
text: Nature is often hidden, sometimes overcome, seldom extinguished.

author: Bob     Brown
text: We have got some very big problems confronting us and let us not make any mistake about it, human history in the future is fraught with tragedy ... It's only through people making a stand against that tragedy and being doggedly optimistic that we are going to win through. If you look at the plight of the human race it could well tip you into despair, so you have to be very strong.

author: José Saramago
text: Not only does the universe have its own laws, all of them indifferent to the contradictory dreams and desires of humanity, and in the formulation of which we contribute not one iota, apart, that is, from the words by which we clumsily name them, but everything seems to indicate that it uses these laws for aims and objectives that transcend and always will transcend our understanding.

author: Alexander Pope
text: True wit is nature to advantage dressed;What oft was thought, but ne'er so well expressed.

author: Jane Austen
text: When I look out on such a night as this, I feel as if there could be neither wickedness nor sorrow in the world; and there certainly would be less of both if the sublimity of Nature were more attended to, and people were carried more out of themselves by contemplating such a scene.

author: Thomas Hood
text: I saw old Autumn in the misty mornStand shadowless like silence, listeningTo silence, for no lonely bird would singInto his hollow ear from woods forlorn,Nor lowly hedge nor solitary thorn; --Shaking his languid locks all dewy brightWith tangled gossamer that fell by night,Pearling his coronet of golden corn.

author: Marquis de Sade
text: Let us give ourselves indiscriminately to everything our passions suggest, and we will always be happy…Conscience is not the voice of Nature but only the voice of prejudice.

author: John Fowles
text: The moon hung over the planet Earth, a dead thing over a dying thing.

author: Edward Abbey
text: What is the purpose of the giant sequoia tree? The purpose of the giant sequoia tree is to provide shade for the tiny titmouse.

author: Augustus
text: If we could survive without a wife, citizens of Rome, all of us would do without that nuisance; but since nature has so decreed that we cannot manage comfortably with them, nor live in any way without them, we must plan for our lasting preservation rather than for our temporary pleasure.

author: Ernst Haeckel
text: Civilisation and the life of nations are governed by the same laws as prevail throughout nature and organic life.

author: Anton Chekhov
text: When describing nature, a writer should seize upon small details, arranging them so that the reader will see an image in his mind after he closes his eyes. For instance: you will capture the truth of a moonlit night if you'll write that a gleam like starlight shone from the pieces of a broken bottle, and then the dark, plump shadow of a dog or wolf appeared. You will bring life to nature only if you don't shrink from similes that liken its activities to those of human

author: George Santayana
text: Everything in nature is lyrical in its ideal essence, tragic in its fate, and comic in its existence.

author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
text: There is eloquence in the tonguelesswind, and a melody in the flowing brooks and the rustling of thereeds beside them, which by their inconceivable relation to somethingwithin the soul, awaken the spirits to a dance of breathlessrapture, and bring tears of mysterious tenderness to the eyes, likethe enthusiasm of patriotic success, or the voice of one belovedsinging to you alone.

author: Adriaan Kortlandt

author: Grigoris Deoudis
